home-ops · Claude Code skill

renovate-merge

The skill merges the open Renovate PRs of home-ops one at a time, in a safe sequence. After each merge, Flux applies the change, and the cluster must be healthy before the next merge.

Start it in the home-ops repository with /renovate-merge. Claude Code does not start it without this command.

Who does whatThe loopRisk classesAlways askScriptsGuardsRecoveryThe plan noteFiles and tests

Who does what

Each step goes to the least expensive script or model that can do it correctly. A script makes every decision that the facts can give. A model decides only when the facts alone cannot give the decision.

Scripts

They classify the PRs, examine the checks and the CRDs, merge, wait for Flux, and make backups. Each result is an exit code.

Haiku

The renovate-facts agent reads the release notes of a risky PR. It copies the facts about incompatible changes, upgrade paths and data. It can only read, and it does not decide.

Sonnet

The skill runs on Sonnet. It runs the loop, reads the exit codes, keeps the plan note current, and gives the risky cases to Opus.

Opus

The renovate-escalation agent decides each risky PR and each failure. It acts once: merge, config PR, intermediate version, revert or defer.

You

You decide the cases on the "always ask" list, and the cases where Opus is not sure.

The loop

  1. script wait.sh examines the cluster. If the cluster is not healthy, the loop stops.
  2. script classify.sh gives each open PR its phase, risk class and pair. New PRs get a row in the plan note.
  3. Sonnet takes the next todo row in the sequence: CI, leaf apps, the AI stack, infrastructure, major versions.
  4. Sonnet does the minor PR of a pair before its major PR.
  5. script precheck.sh examines the checks of each PR. For a low or medium row, crd-diff.sh also compares the CRDs. A failure increases the class to review.
  6. Haiku For a review or high row, renovate-facts collects the facts. Then the row goes to you or to Opus, and the loop takes the next row.
  7. script backup.sh makes a backup if the new version can change data.
  8. script merge.sh merges, and wait.sh waits until Flux applies the change and the cluster is healthy.
  9. Sonnet If wait.sh gives 0, Sonnet sets the row to merged. If not, Sonnet stops the loop. It writes the failure in the note and gives it to Opus.
  10. Sonnet At the end, Sonnet gives you the rows with waiting for user.

Risk classes

classify.sh gives the class from the PR title and the changed files. A step of the loop can increase a class. Nothing decreases a class.

ClassWhenWho decides
lowA digest or a patch version of a leaf app or of an AI appSonnet, after the checks
mediumA minor version. Also a digest or a patch of infrastructure, of a CI workflow, or of a data store.Sonnet, after the checks
reviewA major version, or a new year of a calendar version. Also a minor version below 1.0, or a minor version of a data store. Also a title without versions, or a PR with 100 files or more.Opus
highA major version, a new calendar year or a title without versions of a data store. Also any change to the platform or to secrets.You, for a row with the "always ask" mark. Opus for the other rows.

Always ask the user

Opus does not decide these cases, because an error can lose data or stop the cluster.

  • A major version of a data store: Postgres, Dragonfly, Ceph, OpenEBS, VolSync, Kopia, or an app database.
  • Any change to the platform (Talos, Kubernetes, Flux) or to secrets (External Secrets, 1Password Connect).
  • A data migration that a person must do: an export and an import, pg_upgrade, or a migration command. An app that migrates its database when it starts is not on this list, but backup.sh runs first.
  • A restore of data, or a step that deletes a PVC.
  • A change to credentials.
  • A revert after the new version started, if the new version migrates its database when it starts.

Scripts

The scripts are in .claude/skills/renovate-merge/scripts/. Run them with bash from the repository root. The decisions are in renovate_lib.py, which has unit tests.

ScriptExit codes
classify.sh0 done · 1 the PR list can be incomplete
wait.sh <sha> <merged_at> [timeout]0 healthy · 1 failure in the cluster · 2 timeout · 3 the script cannot read the cluster
precheck.sh <pr>0 ready · 10 not ready yet, run again later · 20 not mergeable · 30 checks fail
crd-diff.sh <pr>0 no CRD change · 3 Flux applies the new CRDs · 4 Flux does not apply them · 2 the script cannot read them
backup.sh <namespace> <app> [--postgres]0 backups complete · 1 failure · 3 no data to copy · 4 the hourly VolSync schedule can stay off
merge.sh <pr> [--own] [--user-approved]0 merged, with sha=… merged_at=… · 1 no merge · 2 Flux did not fetch · 3 merged, commit unknown · 5 a guard refused

precheck.sh ignores two failures on purpose. The lint jobs fail because of style errors that are already on main. A flux-local job that fails only at "Add Comment" renders correctly. Its diff is too long for a PR comment.

Exit code 64 is a wrong call. Run backup.sh in the background: a backup can take 30 minutes.

Recovery

  • Recover through git only. Flux applies the state in git again. Thus it cancels a helm rollback or a kubectl edit.
  • To undo a merge: gh pr revert <pr>, then merge.sh --own and wait.sh. Then close the PR that Renovate opens again for the same version.
  • A config change that a Renovate PR needs goes in a separate PR to main. GitHub refuses a push to a renovate/* branch.
  • If the release notes require an intermediate version, Opus opens a PR for that version first. Renovate then rebases its own PR.

Guards in the code

The rules of the skill are text for a model. Text can fail, so merge.sh makes the important rules hard. A model cannot argue with these checks.

  • merge.sh merges only a PR from the Renovate bot. With --own, it merges a PR of the skill that changes only versions or the CRD policy.
  • It refuses a PR with the "always ask" mark without --user-approved. Only the main session gives this flag, after your approval in the conversation.
  • It runs precheck.sh again, and it merges only the commit that precheck.sh examined.
  • The skill and the agents cannot run gh pr merge, kubectl apply, kubectl edit, helm rollback or op directly.
  • The renovate-facts agent has no shell. Text from PRs and release notes is data that nobody examined, so no agent obeys an instruction in it.

The plan note

The note 10 - Projects/home-ops/Renovate merge plan <YYYY-MM>.md in the notes vault holds the state. The skill reads and changes it only through the notes MCP server. Each PR has one row with its class and its status: todo, merged, waiting for user, deferred or closed. The skill saves the note after each change, so a later session can continue. The workstation commits and pushes the vault.
